title: Python SDK: rewindable stream iterator, pluggable error policies, and per-event telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a rewindable/seekable streaming chat iterator to the Python SDK, along with a pluggable error-policy API and consistent per-event telemetry tags so consumers can safely resume, rewind, or skip bad events without losing conversation context.
background: We have multiple customer-reported cases where streaming chat connections produce transient malformed events or partial token batches. Teams either implement fragile ad-hoc replay logic or drop to non-streaming calls. Existing SDK iterators are single-pass and provide limited hooks for backpressure and retry. This ticket proposes a first-class iterator that supports lightweight rewind (by watermark), a policy interface for error handling (retry, skip, rewind-to-watermark, drain-and-fail), and automatic telemetry enrichment for every emitted event.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement RewindableStreamIterator: an iterator wrapper that annotates every chunk with a monotonically increasing watermark (opaque string) and preserves a small ring-buffer window to allow rewind to recent watermarks. 2) Expose ErrorPolicy base class and built-in policies (RetryPolicy with exponential backoff and token-aware retry limits, SkipPolicy, RewindPolicy). 3) Add per-event telemetry tags (stream_id, watermark, model_variant, latency_ms, event_kind) emitted via existing telemetry hooks. 4) Provide clear ergonomic examples showing common consumer patterns: resume-after-network-error, compacting partial events, and rewinding to re-run eval hooks.
api_surface:
- class RewindableStreamIterator:  __aiter__(), __anext__(), rewind(watermark: str), current_watermark() -> str, peek() -> Optional[Event]  
- class ErrorPolicy(BaseErrorPolicy): on_error(event_meta, exc) -> PolicyDecision  
- builtin policies: RetryPolicy(max_attempts:int, backoff_strategy:str), SkipPolicy(), RewindPolicy(target_watermark:str)
- telemetry: StreamEvent.add_telemetry(tags: Dict[str,str]) (SDK will populate tags automatically)
acceptance_criteria: RewindableStreamIterator implemented and exported in python SDK package
Iterator preserves a configurable ring buffer and supports rewind(watermark) to any retained watermark
ErrorPolicy interface defined with at least three builtin policies: RetryPolicy, SkipPolicy, RewindPolicy
Per-event telemetry tags are present and emitted through existing telemetry channel for all streaming events
Unit tests covering: normal streaming, rewind behavior, buffer eviction semantics, retry attempts, skip behavior, and telemetry enrichment
Integration test demonstrates resume after simulated network drop and rewind to previous watermark to replay tokens
Documentation page with cookbook patterns (resume, rewind-to-correct-structured-output, graceful-skip) and 3 short code examples
design_notes: Watermark should be opaque (string) from server; SDK must not interpret it beyond equality and ordering derived from sequence numbers when available
Ring buffer size default: 128 items — tuned for typical short rewinds but not unbounded memory usage; configurable by user via max_buffer_items
Rewind semantics: rewind(wm) moves consumer cursor to first item with watermark >= wm found in buffer; if missing, raise RewindError with hint to request a non-streamed replay endpoint
ErrorPolicy decisions: (retry, skip, rewind, fail). Retry may surface a backoff sleep and will re-attempt reading from underlying stream; policy must be async-friendly
Telemetry should include stream_id and watermark on all synthetic and partial events so downstream observability and debugging tools can correlate replays
Backpressure: RewindableStreamIterator will not buffer unlimited incoming data; it cooperates with underlying socket/backpressure. Provide optional max_inflight_bytes and max_buffer_items.
Performance: avoid copying token buffers when rewinding — store references to original event objects where safe; consider copy-on-write for mutated consumers
implementation_tasks: Implement RewindableStreamIterator class with ring buffer, async iterator protocol, rewind(), peek(), and watermarks
Wire SDK core stream client to produce watermarks on events and attach telemetry keys
Implement builtin policies: RetryPolicy, SkipPolicy, RewindPolicy and tests
Add unit tests for buffer eviction, rewind missing-watermark behavior, concurrent rewind+consume race cases
Add integration test that simulates malformed event mid-stream and verifies SkipPolicy and telemetry entries
Document API surface in docs/sdk/streaming.md and add example snippets to README
Open PR and link to GH: redwood-inference/sdk-python#TODO
Coordinate with telemetry infra team to ensure tags surface in our observability pipeline
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag STREAM_REWINDABLE=enabled (SDK default: disabled)
2) Publish pre-release wheel with feature flag and examples; solicit beta feedback from 3 internal customers
3) Remove flag and enable by default after 2 weeks of no major issues; ship in sdk-python-0.9.0
risks: Memory blowup if users set very large ring buffer; mitigated by sane defaults and documentation
Server-provided watermarks may not be monotonic for certain model variants — SDK should defensively handle non-monotonic watermarks by falling back to sequence counters
Incorrect rewind semantics could lead to duplicate tokens being re-emitted in ways that confuse consumers; examples must show de-duplication patterns
Telemetry volume increase — need to verify storage/ingest budget for high-frequency streaming customers
